        self.X = X

        self.ln_a = nn.LayerNorm(D)

        self.k = nn.Linear(D, D)

analyses.4: All 18 trials scored 0, both on dev and in training. Ruled out so far: type-major and type-minor frames under sets A and B; obs under 8 symmetries combined with A or B; LayerNorm with small outputs; dense all-action heads, which allow any index order or a moved DONE; and a separate critic with gamma 0.99. One mechanism none of these tested is reward scale. If rewards are much larger than described, value-loss gradients dominate the single global gradient-norm clip (1.0), so the policy gets almost no update. A separate critic does not avoid this, because the clip is shared. Scaling the value gradient by 0.01 in the forward pass avoids it. Adam rescales each parameter's step, so the critic itself still learns. I add this to every candidate as a cheap hedge. The candidates then pair it with known frame sets, with cross-attention (which can learn any cell correspondence, including rolls) and with channel-last obs readings. This is the last round, so I am optimising for any nonzero score rather than for clean attribution.
